walkthroughs.body_html:
Aspects of Political Life in the German-speaking World — a core area of A-Level German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Aspects of Political Life in the German-speaking World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Aspects of Political Life in the German-speaking World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Where does the verb go after 'weil'?
options: second position
first position
end of the clause
before subject

mcqs.q: When does 'in' take the accusative vs dative?
options: It always takes the same case.
Accusative for movement INTO a place; dative for location IN a place.
Ich fahre zu Deutschland.
It depends on the speaker's mood.

mcqs.q: How does 'der Mann' change in the accusative case?
options: Der Mann (unchanged).
Ich fahre zu Deutschland.
Den Mann.
Dem Mann.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I'm travelling to Germany' in German?
options: Dem Mann.
Ich fahre zu Deutschland.
Ich fahre nach Deutschland.
Ich fahre in Deutschland.
